vacuum exposure time is a critical factor to control the pore size of TM membranes and thus their MW cut-off performance and water flux.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of titania membranes with a high rejection of oil emulsified water and a good water flux.
the synthesis and characterization of titania membranes with a controlled pore size for water purification and oil/water separations.
the synthesis and characterization of TM membranes for water treatment applications, including oil/water separation and MW cut-off.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

vacuum exposure times between 30 and >300 s would be recommended for the synthesis of TiO2 membranes with high water fluxes and excellent rejection for the separation of PVP-360kDa molecules and oil emulsions.
the TM membranes are suitable for water treatment and oil/water emulsions separation.
a vacuum exposure time of 600 s would provide a TM membrane with an optimal balance between water flux and MW cut-off performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the vacuum exposure time of the titania membranes can be tailored to control the molecular weight cutoff and structural properties, which can be used for water treatment applications such as the separation of oil from water.
a mechanism of tailoring the pore size of titania membranes was achieved by controlling the TiO2 particle size through vacuum exposure time.
the vacuum-assisted TM membranes can be used for water processing, and the vacuum exposure time can be tuned to achieve a specific molecular cut-off performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MW cut-off performance of titania membranes can be controlled by vacuum exposure time, thus allowing for the development of tailored titania membranes for specific MW cut-off performance.
a simple vacuum exposure step is an effective and inexpensive method for tailoring the pore structure of titania membranes to achieve high MW cut-off and oil/water filtration performance.
vacuum-assisted TM membranes can be prepared in a simple and cost-effective way to achieve MW cut-off performance and separation efficiency for oil/water emulsions.
